To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the thermostability differences between the A:U- and G:C-based polypurine-polypyrimidine duplexes disappear on the insertion of the amino group into position-2 of the purine bases.
the 2-aminopurine base-pair is less thermostable than the guanine base-pair and the difference between the thermostability is not due to the particular nucleotide sequence.
the 2-aminopurine base-pair has the lowest thermostability among all known base-pairs and that it is the only one that destabilizes B-DNA.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the unusual properties of the n2A-containing DNA duplexes.
the influence of the 2-amino group on the structure and thermostability of B-DNAs.
the unusual contribution of 2-amino group to the thermostabilization and destabilization of the double helix.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the presence of 2- aminoadenine in DNA is a disadvantage for thermostabilization.
the 2-aminopurine base in DNA has an unusual effect on its thermostability.
the 2-aminopurine base-pair is not as thermostable as G:C.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the amino group in position 2 of purines is an unusual structural element in the B-DNA.
2-aminopurines are not thermostability-promoting bases in DNA.
the amino group at position 2 of purines is a destabilizing element for the B-DNA structure.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the 5-substituents in pyrimidines and the 2-substituents of purines are of equal importance for the thermostabilization.
the unusual contribution of the n2A base to the thermostabilization is due to its unique structural properties and not the consequence of its chemical modification.
the 2-amino group is a very important factor in the thermostabilization and stabilization of the DNA duplexes.
